newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Diffs mixed in spotty trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Diffs mixed in spotty trade.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices were mixed late Monday amid stable differentials on the Gulf Coast, strengthening conventional unleaded in the Midwest's Group Three market, and weaker values in New York Harbor, players said.

Activity was extremely scant in all centers, but Gulf Coast diffs managed to hold their own ahead of Tuesday's deadline for scheduling some back-13th-cycle deliveries on the Colonial Pipeline, players said.
"It didn't look like anybody did anything today. It was slow as molasses," said one Gulf player, who predicted the pace would pick up nicely Tuesday.
"I think you'll see some stuff start moving Tuesday," he said, with arrival of the deadline for nominating back-13th cycle shipments of heating oil and high sulfur diesel on the Colonial.

USG heating oil was offered at 2.25 cents below the June print, unchanged from late Friday diffs, players said. And low sulfur diesel parcels were sold for 0.85 cent and 0.90 cent under the June screen -- also stable with late last week.
Gulf unleaded gasoline, meanwhile, was offered at 4.0 cents below the print, little changed.

NYMEX activity failed to stir the sleepy cash market, with June NYMEX gasoline settling a negligible 0.02 cent higher at 60.54 cents a gallon and June heating oil eking out a scant 0.03 cent gain to 53.05 cents.

In the Group Three market, traders said diffs on conventional unleaded jumped one cent on continuing tight supplies attributed to maintenance last month on the Explorer Pipeline, with deals heard done at 3.00 cents over June NYMEX..
In New York Harbor, heating oil was offered at 2.75 cents above June futures late day, stable with midday but a half cent weaker than Friday diffs.
Traders said diffs eased soon after Sun Co lowered its posted price Monday morning. Diffs held at the lower levels througout the day, traders said, as buyers remained on the sidelines.
NYH low sulfur diesel was offered at 3.25 cents over, a half cent weaker than Friday diffs, with material offered at 2.50 cents over the June print for deliveries by May 10, traders added.
